title: Backstage Pass
theme: Behind the scenes: cast member lingo and park operations
intro: [whispers] Psst. Come on in, nobody's looking. [excited] Welcome to BACKSTAGE PASS, where we sneak behind the curtain at Disney: cast member lingo, secret tunnels and how the magic really works!

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A half-open backstage door glowing with golden light, revealing a glimpse of a colourful theme park street beyond, while the dim backstage corridor is full of costume racks, tool carts and coiled cables.

categories.title: Saving Mr. Banks
categories.intro: Our film category is the ultimate behind-the-scenes movie: Saving Mr. Banks, all about the making of Mary Poppins. [chuckles] Spoonful of sugar not included.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A 1960s Hollywood studio rehearsal room with an upright piano, scattered sheet music, a black umbrella hooked over a chair, and afternoon sun through venetian blinds.

clues.clue: In Saving Mr. Banks, Tom Hanks plays this famous studio boss who wants to make a movie from a beloved book.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Walt Disney! [laughs] Tom Hanks even grew the moustache. Commitment!

clues.clue: Emma Thompson plays P. L. Travers, the author who created this magical nanny.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Mary Poppins! Practically perfect in every way. [sarcastic] Unlike Mrs. Travers's mood.

clues.clue: In the film, Travers works on the songs with this famous pair of songwriting brothers.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Sherman Brothers! Richard and Robert also wrote It's a Small World. [whispers] Sorry, now it's stuck in your head.

clues.clue: Travers makes a famous demand that this colour must not appear anywhere in the movie.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is red! [gasps] No red at ALL. The Disney team had to get very creative.

clues.clue: Paul Giamatti plays Ralph, the cheerful Los Angeles worker with this job who drives Travers around.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is chauffeur! [chuckles] Ralph is the only person in Hollywood who gets a smile out of her.

categories.title: Speak Like a Cast Member
categories.intro: At Disney, everybody speaks the secret language of show business. [mischievously] Translate these words into cast member lingo!

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A cozy backstage break room with a long row of lockers, a cork bulletin board with blank paper notes, a pair of spotless shoes on a bench and a cup of coffee steaming.

clues.clue: At Disney parks, people who come to visit aren't called customers. They're called this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is guests! [excited] Because you're not buying a ticket... you're visiting someone's home.

clues.clue: Disney park employees are called this, because they're part of the show.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is cast members! Every single one of them, from the ride operator to the street sweeper.

clues.clue: Cast members don't wear uniforms. Instead, Disney calls their outfits these.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is costumes! [laughs] Even if your costume is a polo shirt and a name tag.

clues.clue: Fences and walls Disney wants you to ignore are painted a dull colour nicknamed Go Away this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is green! Go Away Green. [whispers] If you've never noticed it... it's working.

clues.clue: Disney's rules for cast member hair, makeup and grooming are called The Disney this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Look! The Disney Look. [chuckles] And yes, it has been updated over the years, so relax.

categories.title: Behind the Berm
categories.intro: It's a picture category! Each image shows a secret trick Imagineers use to make the magic. [dramatic pause] Name the trick.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A cutaway view of a grassy embankment surrounding a theme park, with railroad tracks along the top, a sunny storybook village inside and a busy gray highway hidden outside.

clues.clue: Look closely! Three circles hidden in this rock wall make a secret shape fans hunt for all over the parks. What's it called?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is a Hidden Mickey! [excited] Once you start finding them, you'll NEVER stop.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A rough stone wall in warm sunlight where three round mossy stones, one large and two smaller on top, form a subtle mouse-head silhouette hidden among other stones.

clues.clue: This classic illusion uses angled glass to make see-through ghosts dance in a haunted ballroom.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Pepper's ghost! It's a stage trick from the 1860s. [mischievously] Ghosts have been reflecting on their lives for a LONG time.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A dim Victorian ballroom seen from a high balcony, faint translucent glowing figures of light dancing above the floor, a giant sheet of glass angled in the foreground catching reflections.

clues.clue: Disneyland is surrounded by this raised wall of earth and trees, so guests can't see the outside world.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the berm! Walt wanted guests to forget the real world. [chuckles] And the train rides on top of it.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A tall grassy embankment covered with trees and shrubs, a small steam railroad track running along its top, seen from inside a sunny park.

clues.clue: This Imagineering device puffs scents like vanilla and fresh cookies into the air.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Smellitzer! [laughs] Ever wonder why you suddenly crave cookies on Main Street? Now you know.

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A small brass cannon-shaped device hidden in leafy bushes, puffing a soft swirl of glowing mist toward a cobblestone street with a bakery window.

clues.clue: Magic Kingdom whisks trash away through underground pneumatic tubes in this system known by a four-letter acronym.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is AVAC! Garbage zooms through the tubes at around 60 miles per hour. [gasps] Faster than some rides!

media.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A clean industrial tunnel with large silver pneumatic tubes curving along the ceiling, pressure gauges and valves, soft blue utility lighting.

categories.title: Operation Magic
categories.intro: Now for the rules of running a theme park. [chuckles] Some of these will make you say, WAIT, really?

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. An empty theme park street at dawn just before opening, a velvet rope stretched across it, a pushcart, a broom leaning on a lamppost and soft pink morning light.

clues.clue: To keep sidewalks clean, Disney World and Disneyland famously don't sell this sticky treat.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is chewing gum! [laughs] Walt did not want to scrape it off his streets.

clues.clue: Instead of pointing with one finger, cast members point with an open hand or using this many fingers.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is two! The famous Disney point. [chuckles] Some say it started because one finger can seem rude in some cultures.

clues.clue: Besides their first name, a cast member's name tag often lists this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is their hometown! It's a great conversation starter. [excited] Oh, you're from Ohio TOO?

clues.clue: Magic Kingdom sits on top of these tunnels that let cast members move around unseen.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the utilidors! [whispers] Technically they're at ground level, and the park is built on top. Sneaky.

clues.clue: Disneyland's exclusive members-only club, hidden in New Orleans Square, is called Club this number.
clues.reveal: [dramatic pause] The correct answer is 33! Club 33. [sighs] And no, I have NOT been invited. Yet.

categories.title: Imagineering Insiders
categories.intro: Our fan category: the people and words behind the magic. [excited] True Disney nerds, this one's for YOU.

art.prompt: Original painterly digital illustration, 16:9, cinematic lighting, rich saturated colour, no people, no characters, no logos, no text or lettering. A cluttered Imagineering drafting table with pencil sketches of castles and rides, clay models, a desk lamp and a corkboard of unlabelled concept art.

clues.clue: Disney calls the areas guests can see, like park streets and rides, this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is onstage! [chuckles] And everything you can't see? Backstage. Just like a theater.

clues.clue: Walt used this hot-dog nickname for a big landmark, like a castle, that pulls guests down the street.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is wienie! [laughs] Walt said it works like waving a hot dog in front of a puppy.

clues.clue: Walt Disney Imagineering started out with this name, made from Walt's initials.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is WED Enterprises! W, E, D for Walter Elias Disney.

clues.clue: This longtime Imagineering leader wrote Mickey's Ten Commandments, rules for great theme park design.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Marty Sklar! [excited] Rule number one? Know your audience. Rule number two? Wear your guests' shoes.

clues.clue: Disney's famous Traditions orientation class for new cast members was started by this man in 1955.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Van France! He trained the very first Disneyland cast. [chuckles] Before that, nobody knew what a wienie was.
